title: Laki fissure eruption
summary: The Laki fissure in southern Iceland opened on 8 June 1783 and erupted until February 1784, producing roughly 14.7 to 15 km³ of lava. Gases from the eruption caused a dry fog over Europe from about 16 June 1783, and by 1785 about a fifth of Iceland's population had died of hunger and disease, along with much of its livestock.

uncertainty.note: Start 8 June 1783; Kleemann gives 7 February 1784 as the end, GeoExPro gives February 1784.

where.historical_name: Laki fissure, Iceland under the Danish crown

importance.justification: The largest recorded lava output in historic time, followed by famine in Iceland and a haze over Europe.
